metadata.title: Forking and stability in the representations of a $C^*$-algebra

extraction_notes.note: Corollary 2.5's proof and the existence step cite Fact \ref{HensonsLemma}, a label never defined in the source; Henson's lemma is not stated in the paper, so no node or edge for it.
Remark 4.8 only recalls what 'disjoint' representations are, so it is typed definition rather than remark.

The type relations $\perp^a$, $\perp$ and $\vartriangleright$, the theory $T_\pi$ and the monster model $\tilde H$ are used without definition in the paper (domination is deferred to Buechler), so these symbols have no definition nodes.

The introduction restates prior results and the paper's main results; per the repeated-statement rule the formal copies (Theorem 4.3, Theorems 3.8-4.19) are kept, and Henson-Iovino's stability (stated twice) is kept at its first, introductory occurrence.
Remark 3.2 asserts three equivalences 'easy to see' and is cited as a result; kept as remark (semi_formal) following its environment.

nodes.name: nondegenerate representation $\pi$ of a unital $C^*$-algebra
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a unital $C^*$-algebra and let $\pi:\mathcal{A}\to B(H)$ be a $C^*$-algebra nondegenerate isometric homomorphism, where $B(H)$ is the algebra of bounded operators over a Hilbert space $H$.
nodes.statement_short: Standing setting: $\pi$ is a nondegenerate isometric representation of a unital $C^*$-algebra $\mathcal{A}$ on a Hilbert space $H$.

nodes.name: metric structure of a Hilbert space expanded by a $C^*$-algebra
nodes.statement: Recall that we include a symbol $\dot{a}$ in the language of the Hilbert space structure whose interpretation in $H$ will be $\pi(a)$ for every $a$ in the unit ball of $\mathcal{A}$ getting the following metric structure of only one sort: \[(Ball_1(H),0,-,i,\half[x+y],\|\cdot\|,(\pi(a))_{a\in Ball_1(\mathcal{A})})\] where $Ball_1(H)$ and $Ball_1(\mathcal{A})$ are the corresponding unit balls in $H$ and $\mathcal{A}$ respectively; $0$ is the zero vector in $H$; $-: Ball_1(H)\to Ball_1(H)$ is the function that to any vector $v\in Ball_1(H)$ assigns the vector $-v$; $i: Ball_1(H)\to Ball_1(H)$ is the function that to any vector $v\in Ball_1(H)$ assigns the vector $iv$ where $i^2=-1$; $\half[x+y]: Ball_1(H)\times Ball_1(H)\to Ball_1(H)$ is the function that to a couple of vectors $v$, $w\in Ball_1(H)$ assigns the vector $\half[v+w]$; $\|\cdot\|: Ball_1(H) \to [0, 1]$ is the norm function; $\mathcal{A}$ is an unital $C^*$-algebra; $\pi:\mathcal{A}\to B(H)$ is a $C^*$-algebra isometric homomorphism.
nodes.origin_citation: Argoty, The model theory of modules of a C*-algebra
nodes.statement_short: One-sorted continuous-logic structure on the unit ball of $H$ with the Hilbert space operations and a symbol for $\pi(a)$ for each $a$ in the unit ball of $\mathcal{A}$.

nodes.name: Henson-Iovino stability of Hilbert spaces with bounded operators
nodes.statement: In \cite{Io}, Henson and Iovino, observed that the theory of a Hilbert space expanded with a family of bounded operators is stable.
assumptions: a Hilbert space expanded with a family of bounded operators
conclusions: is stable

nodes.name: generic automorphisms of a Hilbert space (Ben Yaacov-Usvyatsov-Zadka)
nodes.statement: In \cite{BUZ} Ben Yaacov, Usvyatsov and Zadka characterized the unitary operators corresponding to generic automorphisms of a Hilbert space as those unitary transformations whose spectrum is $S^1$ and gave the key ideas used in this paper to characterize domination and orthogonality of types.
nodes.statement_short: Unitary operators giving generic automorphisms of a Hilbert space are exactly those with spectrum $S^1$.
conclusions: characterized the unitary operators corresponding to generic automorphisms of a Hilbert space as those unitary transformations whose spectrum is $S^1$

nodes.name: subrepresentation generated by a set and associated projections
nodes.statement: Given $E\subseteq H$ and $v\in H$, we denote by: \begin{itemize} \item $H_E$, the Hilbert subspace of $H$ generated by the elements $\pi(a)v$, where $v\in E$ and $a\in\mathcal{A}$. \item $\pi_E:=\{\pi(a)\upharpoonright H_E\ |\ a\in \mathcal{A}\}$. \item $(H_E,\pi_E)$, the subrepresentation of $(H,\pi)$ generated by $E$. \item $H_v$, the space $H_E$ when $E=\{v\}$ for some vector $v\in H$. \item $\pi_v:=\pi_E$ when $E=\{v\}$. \item $(H_v,\pi_v)$, the subrepresentation of $(H,\pi)$ generated by $v$. \item $(H,\pi,v)$, means that $\{\pi(a)v\ |\ a\in\mathcal{A}\}$ is dense in $(H,\pi)$. \item $H_E^\perp$, the orthogonal complement of $H_E$. \item $P_E$, the projection over $H_E$. \item $P_{E^\perp}$, the projection over $H_E^\perp$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Notation: $H_E$ the closed span of $\pi(a)v$ for $v\in E$, the subrepresentation $(H_E,\pi_E)$, $H_v$, cyclic triples $(H,\pi,v)$, and projections $P_E$, $P_{E^\perp}$.
nodes.label: DefinitionHv

nodes.name: essential and discrete parts
nodes.statement: Given a representation $\pi:\mathcal{A}\to B(H)$, we define: \begin{itemize} \item The \textit{essential part} of $\pi$ is the $C^*$-algebra homomorphism, \[\pi_e:=\rho\circ\pi:\mathcal{A}\to B(H)/\mathcal{K}(H)\] of $\pi(\mathcal{A})$, where $\rho$ is the canonical proyection of $B(H)$ onto the Calkin Algebra $B(H)/\mathcal{K}(H)$. \item The \textit{discrete part} of $\pi$ is the restriction, \begin{align*} \pi_d:ker(\pi_e)&\to \mathcal{K}(H)\\ a &\to \pi(a) \end{align*} \item The \textit{discrete part} of $\pi(\mathcal{A})$ is defined in the following way: \[\pi(\mathcal{A})_d:=\pi(\mathcal{A})\cap \mathcal{K}(H).\] \item The \textit{essential part} of $\pi(\mathcal{A})$ is the image $\pi(\mathcal{A})_e$ of $\pi(\mathcal{A})$ in the Calkin Algebra. \item The \textit{essential part} of $H$ is defined in the following way: \[H_e:=\text{ker}(\pi(\mathcal{A})_d)\] \item The \textit{discrete part} of $H$ is defined in the following way: \[H_d:=\text{ker}(\pi(\mathcal{A})_d)^\perp\] \item The \textit{essential part} of a vector $v\in H$ is the projection $v_e$ of $v$ over $H_e$. \item The \textit{discrete part} of a vector $v\in H$ is the projection $v_d$ of $v$ over $H_d$. \item The \textit{essential part} of a set $E\subseteq H$ is the set \[E_e:=\{v_e\ |\ v\in E\}\] \item The \textit{discrete part} of a set $G\subseteq H$ is the set \[E_d:=\{v_d\ |\ v\in G\}\] \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Essential and discrete parts of $\pi$, $\pi(\mathcal{A})$, $H$, vectors and sets, via the Calkin algebra and the compact operators in $\pi(\mathcal{A})$.

nodes.name: automorphisms of $(H,\pi)$ fixing $E$
nodes.statement: Let $E\subseteq H$, $U\in \ensuremath{\text{Aut}}(H,\pi)$. Then $U\in \ensuremath{\text{Aut}}((H,\pi)/E)$ if and only if: \begin{itemize} \item For all $v\in H$ and all $a\in\mathcal{A}$, $U(\pi(a)(v))=\pi(a)(Uv)$. \item For all $w\in H_E$, $Uw=w$. \end{itemize}
conclusions: $U\in \ensuremath{\text{Aut}}((H,\pi)/E)$ if and only if: \begin{itemize} \item For all $v\in H$ and all $a\in\mathcal{A}$, $U(\pi(a)(v))=\pi(a)(Uv)$. \item For all $w\in H_E$, $Uw=w$. \end{itemize}
nodes.label: Aut(H/E)

nodes.statement: For any index set $I$, $(H,\pi)\equiv (H,\pi)\oplus(H_e,\pi_e)$.
conclusions: $(H,\pi)\equiv (H,\pi)\oplus(H_e,\pi_e)$

nodes.name: vectors in $H_e$ are not algebraic over $\emptyset$
nodes.statement: Let $v\in H_e$. Then $v$ is not algebraic over $\emptyset$.
conclusions: $v$ is not algebraic over $\emptyset$
nodes.label: Henotalgebraicoveremptyset

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.6
nodes.statement: Let $\kappa>2^{\aleph_0}$ and consider $(H,\pi)\oplus\bigoplus_{i\in I}(H_e,\pi_e)$. By Corollary \ref{CoroElementaryEquivalent}. Then there are $\kappa$ vectors $v_i$ for $i<\kappa$ such that every $v_i$ has the same type over $\emptyset$ as $v$. This means that the orbit of $v$ under the automorphisms of $(H,\pi)$ is unbounded and therefore $v$ is not algebraic over the emptyset.
nodes.statement_short: Add $\kappa>2^{\aleph_0}$ copies of $(H_e,\pi_e)$ (elementarily equivalent by Cor. 2.5) to get unboundedly many realizations of $tp(v/\emptyset)$.

nodes.name: vectors in $H_d$ are algebraic over $\emptyset$
nodes.statement: Let $v\in H_d$. Then $v$ is algebraic over $\emptyset$.
conclusions: $v$ is algebraic over $\emptyset$

nodes.name: nonzero essential part implies non-algebraic
nodes.statement: Let $v\in H$ such that $v_e\neq 0$. Then $v$ is not algebraic over $\emptyset$.
conclusions: $v$ is not algebraic over $\emptyset$
nodes.label: LemmaIfVeNotZeroVNotAlgebraic

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.8
nodes.statement: Clear from previous Lemma \ref{Henotalgebraicoveremptyset}.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from Lemma 2.6.

nodes.name: algebraic closure of the empty set
nodes.statement: $acl(\emptyset)=H_d$
conclusions: $acl(\emptyset)=H_d$
nodes.label: aclemptyset

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.9
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{Hdsubsetalgebraicclosureofemptyset}, $H_d\subseteq acl(\emptyset)$ and, by Lemma \ref{LemmaIfVeNotZeroVNotAlgebraic}, $acl(\emptyset)\subseteq H_d$.
nodes.statement_short: Double inclusion from Fact 2.7 and Lemma 2.8.

nodes.name: algebraic closure of a set
nodes.statement: Let $E\subseteq H$. Then $acl(E)$ is the Hilbert subspace of $H$ generated by $dcl(E)$ and $acl(\emptyset)$.
conclusions: $acl(E)$ is the Hilbert subspace of $H$ generated by $dcl(E)$ and $acl(\emptyset)$
nodes.label: aclE

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.10
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be the Hilbert subspace of $H$ generated by $dcl(E)$ and $acl(\emptyset)$. It is clear that $G\subseteq acl(E)$. Let $v\in acl(E)$. By Lemma \ref{Hdsubsetalgebraicclosureofemptyset}, $v_d\in acl(\emptyset)$, and by Theorem \ref{definclosure} and Lemma \ref{Henotalgebraicoveremptyset}, $v_e\in dcl(E)\setminus acl(\emptyset)$. Then $v_e\in dcl(E)$ and $acl(E)\subseteq G$.
nodes.statement_short: Double inclusion: split $v\in acl(E)$ into discrete part (in $acl(\emptyset)$) and essential part (in $dcl(E)$).

nodes.name: independence $\ind^*$
nodes.statement: Let $E$, $F$, $G\subseteq H$. We say that $E$ is \textit{independent} from $G$ over $F$ if for all $v\in E$ $P_{acl(F)}(v)=P_{acl(F\cup G)}(v)$ and denote it $E\ind^*_F G$.
nodes.statement_short: $E\ind^*_F G$ iff projecting each $v\in E$ onto $acl(F)$ and onto $acl(F\cup G)$ gives the same vector.
nodes.label: AindependentB

nodes.name: independence via orthogonality of generated subspaces
nodes.statement: Let $\bar v$, $\bar w\in H^n$ and $E\subseteq H$. Then it is easy to see that: \begin{itemize} \item $\bar v$ is independent from $\bar w$ over $\emptyset$ if and only if for every $j,k=1,\dots,n$, $H_{(v_j)_e}\perp H_{(w_k)_e}$. \item $\bar v$ is independent from $\bar w$ over $E$ if and only if for every $j,k=1,\dots,n$, $H_{P_E^\perp(v_j)_e}\perp H_{P_E^\perp(w_k)_e}$. \item $\bar v\in H^n$ and $E$, $F\subseteq H$. Then $\bar v\ind^*_EF$ if and only if for every $j=1,\dots,n$ $v_j\ind^*_EF$ that is, for all $j=1,\dots,n$ $P_{acl(E)}(v_j)=P_{acl(E\cup F)}(v_j)$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Independence of tuples reduces to orthogonality of the cyclic subspaces generated by the essential parts, and to independence of each coordinate.
nodes.label: independenceoverempty

nodes.name: types over $\emptyset$ are determined by cyclic subrepresentations
nodes.statement: Let $v$, $w\in\tilde{H}$. Then $tp(v/\emptyset)=tp(w/\emptyset)$ if and only if $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$, this is, the map sending $v$ to $w$ extends to a unique isometric isomorphism between $(H_v,\pi_v)$ and $(H_w,\pi_w)$.
conclusions: $tp(v/\emptyset)=tp(w/\emptyset)$ if and only if $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$
nodes.label: typeoverempty1

nodes.name: characterization of $\ind^*$-independent extensions
nodes.statement: Let $E\subseteq F\subseteq H$, $p\in S_n(E)$ $q\in S_n(F)$ and $\bar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n)$, $\bar w=(v_1,\dots,v_n)\in H^n$ be such that $p=tp(\bar v/E)$ and $q=tp(\bar w/F)$. Then $q$ is an extension of $p$ such that $\bar w\ind^*_EF$ if and only if the following conditions hold: \begin{enumerate} \item For every $j=1,\dots,n$, $P_{acl(E)}(v_j)=P_{acl(F)}(w_j)$ \item For every $j=1,\dots,n$, $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v_j},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v_j},P^\perp_{acl(E)}v_j)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w_j},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w_j},P^\perp_{acl(F)}w_j)$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $q$ is an $\ind^*$-independent extension of $p$ iff the projections onto the algebraic closures agree and the cyclic representations of the orthogonal parts are isomorphic.
assumptions: $E\subseteq F\subseteq H$, $p\in S_n(E)$ $q\in S_n(F)$ and $\bar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n)$, $\bar w=(v_1,\dots,v_n)\in H^n$ be such that $p=tp(\bar v/E)$ and $q=tp(\bar w/F)$
conclusions: $q$ is an extension of $p$ such that $\bar w\ind^*_EF$ if and only if the following conditions hold
nodes.label: nonforkingextension

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.6
nodes.statement:

Since $v

It is clear that $P_{acl(E)}(v)=P_{acl(F)}(v)=P_{acl(G)}(v)$ so $v\ind_E^*F$ and $v\ind_F^*G$. Then $P_{acl(E)}(v)=P_{acl(G)}(v)$ and $v\ind_E^*G$. \item[Symmetry] It is clear from Remark ef{independenceoverA}. \item[Invariance] Let $U$ be an automorphism of $(H,\pi)$. Let $ ar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n)$,$ ar w=(w_1,\dots,w_n)\in H^n$ and $E\subseteq H$ be such that $ ar v\ind_E^* ar w$. By Remark ef{independenceoverA}, this means that for every $j$, $k=1,\dots,n$ $H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}(v_j)}\perp H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}(w_k)}$. It follows that for every $j$, $k=1,\dots,n$ $H_{P^\perp_{acl(UE)}(Uv_j)}\perp H_{P^\perp_{acl(UE)}(Uw_k)}$ and, again by Remark ef{independenceoverA}, $Uv\ind_{acl(UE)}^*Uw$. \item[Existence] Let $(	ilde{H},	ilde{\pi})$ be the monster model and let $E\subseteq F\subseteq 	ilde{H}$ be small sets. We show, by induction on $n$, that for every $p\in S_n(E)$, there exists $q\in S_n(F)$ such that $q$ is a non-forking extension of $p$.  egin{description} \item[Case $n=1$] Let $v\in 	ilde{H}$ be such that $p=tp(v/E)$ and let $(H^\prime,\pi^\prime,u):=(H_{(P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)},\pi_{(P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)},P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)$. Then, by Fact ef{HensonsLemma}, the model $(\hat{H},\hat{\pi}):=(H,\pi)\oplus (H^\prime,\pi^\prime)$ is an elementary extension of $(H,\pi)$. Let $v^\prime:=P_{acl(E)}v+P^\perp_{acl(E)}v_d+u\in \hat{H}$. Then, by Theorem ef{nonforkingextension}, the type $tp(v^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v/E)$. \item[Induction step] Now, let $ ar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1})\in 	ilde{H}^{n+1}$. By induction hypothesis, there are $v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime\in H$ such that $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n/E)$. Let $U$ be an automorphism of the monster model fixing $E$ pointwise such that for every $j=1,\dots,n$, $U(v_j)=v_j^\prime$. Let $v_{n+1}^\prime\in 	ilde{H}$ be such that $tp(v_{n+1}^\prime/Fv_1^\prime\cdots v_n^\prime)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(U(v_{n+1})/Ev_1^\prime,\cdots v_n^\prime)$. Then, by transitivity, $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime,v_{n+1}^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1}/E)$. \end{description} \item[Stationarity] Let $(	ilde{H},	ilde{\pi})$ be the monster model and let $E\subseteq F\subseteq 	ilde{H}$ be small sets. We show, by induction on $n$, that for every $p\in S_n(E)$, if $q\in S_n(F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $p$ to $F$ then $q=p^\prime$, where $p^\prime$ is the $\ind^*$-independent extension of $p$ to $F$ built in the proof of existence.  egin{description} \item[Case $n=1$] Let $v\in H$ be such that $p=tp(v/E)$, and let $q\in S(F)$ and $w\in H$ be such that $w\models q$. Let $v^\prime$ be as in previous item. Then, by Theorem ef{nonforkingextension} we have that:  egin{enumerate} \item $P_{acl(E)}v=P_{acl(F)}v^\prime=P_{acl(F)}w$ \item $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v},P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to both \[(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},P^\perp_{acl(F)}w)\] and \[(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime)\] \end{enumerate} This means that $P_{acl(F)}v^\prime=P_{acl(F)}w$ and $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},P^\perp_{acl(F)}w)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime)$ and, therefore $q=tp(v^\prime/F)=p^\prime$. \item[Induction step] Let $ ar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1})$, $ ar v^\prime=(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1}^\prime)$ and $ ar w=(w_1,\dots,w_{n+1})\in	ilde{H}$ be such that $ ar v\models p$, $ ar v^\prime\models p^\prime$ and $ ar w\models q$. By transitivity, we have that $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime/F)$ and $tp(w_1,\dots,w_n/F)$ are $\ind^*$-independent extensions of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n/E)$. Again by transitivity, $tp(U^{-1}(v_{n+1}^\prime)/Fv_1\cdots v_n)$ and $tp((U^\prime\circ U)^{-1}(w_{n+1})/Fv_1,\cdots v_n)$ are $\ind^*$-independent extensions of $tp(v_{n+1}/Ev_1,\cdots v_n)$. By the case $n=1$ $tp(U^{-1}(v_{n+1}^\prime)/Fv_1\cdots v_n)=tp((U^\prime\circ U)^{-1}(w_{n+1})/Fv_1,\cdots v_n)$ and therefore $p^\prime=tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime v_{n+1}^\prime/F)=tp(w_1,\dots,w_n,w_{n+1}/F)=q$. \end{description} \end{description}
nodes.statement_short: Verify each axiom of a freeness relation in turn, reducing to 1-tuples. Existence and stationarity go by induction on $n$, building a nonforking extension by adding an orthogonal copy of the cyclic representation via Henson's lemma.

nodes.name: stability via an independence relation
nodes.statement: A first order continuous logic theory $T$ is stable if and only if there is an independence relation $\ind^*$ satisfying local character, finite character of dependence, transitivity, symmetry, invariance, existence and stationarity. In that case the relation $\ind^*$ coincides with non-forking.
nodes.origin_citation: Ben Yaacov, Berenstein, Henson, Usvyatsov, Theorem 14.14
assumptions: A first order continuous logic theory $T$
conclusions: $T$ is stable if and only if there is an independence relation $\ind^*$ satisfying local character, finite character of dependence, transitivity, symmetry, invariance, existence and stationarity
In that case the relation $\ind^*$ coincides with non-forking.
nodes.label: LemmaTstableIffItHasGoodIndependenceRelation

nodes.name: superstability of $T_\pi$
nodes.statement: The theory $T_\pi$ is superstable and the relation $\ind^*$ agrees with non-forking.
conclusions: The theory $T_\pi$ is superstable
the relation $\ind^*$ agrees with non-forking
nodes.label: Tpisuperstable

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.8
nodes.statement: By Fact \ref{LemmaTstableIffItHasGoodIndependenceRelation}, $T_\pi$ is stable and the relation $\ind^*$ agrees with non-forking. To prove superstability, we have to show that for every $\bar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n)\in H$, every $F\subseteq H$ and every $\epsilon>0$, there exist a finite $F_0\subseteq F$ and $\bar v^\prime=(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime)\in H^n$ such that $\|v_j-v_j^\prime\|<\epsilon$ and $v_j^\prime\ind_{F_0}F$ for every $j\leq n$. As in the proof of local character, for $j=1,\dots,n$ let $(\ a_1^{jk},\dots,\ a_{l_k}^{jk})_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}$, $(\ e_1^{jk},\dots,\ e_{l_k}^{jk})_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}$, $w_j:=(P_{acl(E)}(v_j))_e$ and $(w_j^k)_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}$ be such that $w_j^k:=\sum_{s=1}^{l_k}\pi(a_s^{jk})\ e_s^{jk}$ for $k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$, and $w_j^k\to w_j$. For $j=1,\dots,n$, let $K_j\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$ be such that $\|w_j-w_j^{K_j}\|<\epsilon$, let $v_j^\prime:=(P_{acl(E)}v_j)_d+w_j^{K_j}$ and let $F_0^j=\{e_s^k\ |\ k\leq K_j\text{ and }s=1,\dots,l_k\}$. If we define $F_0:=U_{j=1}^nF_0^j$, then for every $j=1,\dots,n$ we have that $v_j^\prime\ind_{F_0}^*F$, $|F_0|<\aleph_0$ and $\|v_j-v_j^\prime\|<\epsilon$.
nodes.statement_short: Stability from Fact 3.7; superstability by approximating each coordinate by finite combinations $\sum\pi(a)e$ of elements of a finite $F_0$.

nodes.name: canonical base
nodes.statement: Recall that a canonical base for a type $p$ is a minimal set over which $p$ does not fork.

nodes.name: canonical bases of types
nodes.statement: Let $\bar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n)\in H^n$ and $E\subseteq H$. Then $Cb(tp(\bar v/E)):=\{(P_Ev_1,\dots,P_Ev_n)\}$ is a canonical base for the type $tp(\bar v/E)$.
conclusions: $Cb(tp(\bar v/E)):=\{(P_Ev_1,\dots,P_Ev_n)\}$ is a canonical base for the type $tp(\bar v/E)$
nodes.label: canonicalbase

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.9
nodes.statement: First of all, we consider the case of a 1-tuple. By Theorem \ref{nonforkingextension} $tp(v/E)$ does not fork over $Cb(tp(v/E))$. Let $(v_k)_{k<\omega}$ a Morley sequence for $tp(v/E)$. We have to show that $P_Ev\in dcl((v_k)_{k<\omega})$. By Theorem \ref{nonforkingextension}, for every $k<\omega$ there is a vector $w_k$ such that $v_k=P_Ev+w_k$ and $w_k\perp acl(\{P_Ev\}\cup\{w_j\ |\ j< k\})$. This means that for every $k<\omega$, $w_k\in H_e$ and for all $j$, $k<\omega$, $H_{w_j}\perp H_{w_k}$. For $k<\omega$, let $v^\prime_k:=\frac{v_1+\cdots+v_k}{n}=P_Ev+\frac{w_1+\cdots+w_k}{n}$. Then for every $k<\omega$, $v^\prime_k\in dcl((v_k)_{k<\omega})$. Since $v^\prime_k\to P_ev$ when $k\to\infty$, we have that $P_Ev\in dcl((v_k)_{k<\omega})$. For the case of a general $n$-tuple, by Remark \ref{RemarkItIsEnoughIndependenceForOneVector}, it is enough to repeat the previous argument in every component of $\bar v$.
nodes.statement_short: For a 1-tuple, averages of a Morley sequence converge to $P_Ev$, so $P_Ev$ is definable from it; then argue coordinatewise.

nodes.name: weak elimination of imaginaries
nodes.statement: The theory $T_\pi$ has weak elimination of imaginaries.
conclusions: The theory $T_\pi$ has weak elimination of imaginaries.

nodes.statement: Clear by previous theorem.

nodes.name: positive functional
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}^\prime$ be the dual space of $\mathcal{A}$. An element $\phi\in\mathcal{A}^\prime$ is called \textit{positive} if $\phi(a)\geq 0$ whenever $a\in\mathcal{A}$ is positive, i.e. there is $b\in\mathcal{A}$ such that $a=b^*b$. The set of positive functionals is denoted by $\mathcal{A}^\prime_+$.

nodes.name: vector functionals are positive
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a $C^*$-algebra of operators on a Hilbert space $H$, and let $v\in H$. Then the function $\phi_v$ on $\mathcal{A}$ such that for every $S\in\mathcal{A}$, $\phi_v(S)=\langle Sv\,|\,v\rangle$ is a positive linear functional.
assumptions: $\mathcal{A}$ be a $C^*$-algebra of operators on a Hilbert space $H$, and let $v\in H$
conclusions: the function $\phi_v$ on $\mathcal{A}$ such that for every $S\in\mathcal{A}$, $\phi_v(S)=\langle Sv\,|\,v\rangle$ is a positive linear functional
nodes.label: vectorsdefinepositivelinearfunctionals

nodes.name: types over $\emptyset$ are determined by vector functionals
nodes.statement: Let $v,w\in H$. Then $tp(v/\emptyset)=tp(w/\emptyset)$ if and only if $\phi_v=\phi_w$, where $\phi_v$ denotes the positive linear functional on $\mathcal{A}$ defined by $v$ as in Lemma \ref{vectorsdefinepositivelinearfunctionals}.
conclusions: $tp(v/\emptyset)=tp(w/\emptyset)$ if and only if $\phi_v=\phi_w$
nodes.label: typeoverempty4

nodes.name: orthogonality and domination of positive functionals
nodes.statement: Let $\phi$ and $\psi$ be positive linear functionals on $\mathcal{A}$. \begin{enumerate} \item They are called \textit{orthogonal} ($\phi\perp\psi$) if $\|\phi-\psi\|=\|\phi\|+\|\psi\|$. \item Also, $\phi$ is called \textit{dominated} by $\psi$ ($\phi\leq\psi$) if there exist $\gamma>0$ such that the functional $\gamma\psi-\phi$ is positive. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $\phi\perp\psi$ iff $\|\phi-\psi\|=\|\phi\|+\|\psi\|$; $\phi\leq\psi$ iff $\gamma\psi-\phi$ is positive for some $\gamma>0$.
nodes.label: relationsbetweenpositivelinearfunctionals

nodes.name: cyclic subrepresentations and domination of functionals
nodes.statement: Let $v,w\in H$. Then $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$ if and only if $\phi_v\leq\phi_w$.
conclusions: $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$ if and only if $\phi_v\leq\phi_w$
nodes.label: HvinHw

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.5
nodes.statement: Suppose $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$. Then there exists a vector $v^\prime\in H_w$ such that $(H_v,\pi_v,v)\simeq (H_{v^\prime},\pi_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$. By Radon Nikodim Theorem for rings of operators (see \cite{Hen}), there exists a bounded positive operator $P:(H_w,\pi_w,w)\to (H_{v^\prime},\pi_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$ such that $Pw=v^\prime$ and $P$ commutes with every element of $\pi_v(\mathcal{A})$. Let $\gamma=\|P\|^2$. Then, for every positive element $a\in\mathcal{A}$, $\phi_{v}(a)=\phi_{v^\prime}(a)=\langle \pi(a)v^\prime\ |\ v^\prime\rangle=\langle \pi(a)Pw\ |\ Pw\rangle=\langle P^*\pi(a)Pw\ |\ w\rangle=\langle \pi(a)\|P\|^2w\ |\ w\rangle\leq \gamma\langle \pi(a)w\ |\ w\rangle=\gamma\phi_{w}(a)$ which means that $\gamma\phi_w-\phi_{v}$ is positive and $\phi_v\leq\phi_w$. The converse is Corollary 3.3.8 in \cite{Pe}.
nodes.statement_short: Forward direction via the Radon-Nikodym theorem for rings of operators, giving $\phi_v\leq\|P\|^2\phi_w$; converse cited from Pedersen.

nodes.name: Gelfand-Naimark-Segal construction
nodes.statement: Let $\phi$ be a positive functional on $\mathcal{A}$. Then there exists a cyclic representation $(H_\phi,\pi_\phi,v_\phi)$ such that for all $a\in\mathcal{A}$, $\phi(a)=\langle \pi_\phi(a)v_\phi|v_\phi\rangle$. This representation is called the \textit{Gelfand-Naimark-Segal construction}.
conclusions: there exists a cyclic representation $(H_\phi,\pi_\phi,v_\phi)$ such that for all $a\in\mathcal{A}$, $\phi(a)=\langle \pi_\phi(a)v_\phi|v_\phi\rangle$
nodes.label: GelfandNaimarkSegal

nodes.name: orthogonal functionals give non-embeddable cyclic representations
nodes.statement: Let $v,w\in H$. If $\phi_v\perp\phi_w$, then $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is not isometrically isomorphic to any subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$.
conclusions: $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is not isometrically isomorphic to any subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$
nodes.label: phivperpphiwnotismoetricallyisomorphic

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.7
nodes.statement: Suppose $\phi_v\perp\phi_w$, and $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$. By Theorem \ref{HvinHw} $\phi_v\leq\phi_w$; let $\gamma>0$ be a real number such that $\gamma\phi_w-\phi_v$ is a bounded positive functional and let $u\in H$ be such that $\phi_u=\gamma\phi_w-\phi_v$, which is possible by GNS Theorem. Then $\phi_v=\gamma\phi_w-\phi_u$, and $\|\phi_w-\phi_v\|=\|\phi_w-\gamma\phi_w+\phi_u\|=\|(1-\gamma)\phi_w+\phi_u\|=|1-\gamma|\|\phi_w\|+\|\phi_u\|\neq \|\phi_w\|+\|\phi_v\|$, but this contradicts $\phi_v\perp\phi_w$.
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: domination $\phi_v\leq\phi_w$ and GNS write $\phi_v=\gamma\phi_w-\phi_u$, so the norm identity for orthogonality fails.

nodes.name: disjoint representations
nodes.statement: Recall that two representations are said to be \textit{disjoint} if they do not have any common subrepresentation up to isometric isomorphism.
differentia: they do not have any common subrepresentation up to isometric isomorphism

nodes.name: disjoint subrepresentations have separating central projection
nodes.statement: Two subrepresentations $(H_1,\pi_1)$, $(H_2,\pi_2)$ of $(H,\pi)$ are disjoint if and only if there is a projection $P$ in $\pi(\mathcal{A})^\prime\cap \pi(\mathcal{A})^{\prime\prime}$ such that if $P_1$ and $P_2$ are the projections on $H_1$ and $H_2$ respectively, we have that $PP_1=P_1$ and $(I-P)P_2=P_2$.
nodes.origin_citation: Connes, Noncommutative geometry, Ch. 5 Sec. 2 Prop. 3
conclusions: are disjoint if and only if there is a projection $P$ in $\pi(\mathcal{A})^\prime\cap \pi(\mathcal{A})^{\prime\prime}$ such that if $P_1$ and $P_2$ are the projections on $H_1$ and $H_2$ respectively, we have that $PP_1=P_1$ and $(I-P)P_2=P_2$
nodes.label: FactDisjointSubrepresentationsHaveDisjointProjections

nodes.name: strong closure equals double commutant
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a $C^*$algebra and $\pi:\mathcal{A}\to B(H)$ a nondegenerate representation of $\mathcal{A}$. Let $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$ be the strong closure of $\pi(\mathcal{A})$. Then $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$ is weakly closed and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}=\mathcal{A}^{\prime\prime}$.
assumptions: $\mathcal{A}$ be a $C^*$algebra and $\pi:\mathcal{A}\to B(H)$ a nondegenerate representation of $\mathcal{A}$
conclusions: $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$ is weakly closed and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}=\mathcal{A}^{\prime\prime}$
nodes.label: FactMMisDoubleCommutantOfPiOfA

nodes.name: Kaplansky density theorem
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a $C^*$-subalgebra of $B(H)$ with strong closure $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$. Then the unit ball $Ball_1(\mathcal{A})$ of $\mathcal{A}$ is strongly dense in the unit ball $Ball_1(\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$ of $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$. Furthermore, the set of selfadjoint elements in $Ball_1(\mathcal{A})$ is strongly dense in the set of selfadjoint elements of $Ball_1(\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$.
assumptions: $\mathcal{A}$ be a $C^*$-subalgebra of $B(H)$ with strong closure $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$
conclusions: the unit ball $Ball_1(\mathcal{A})$ of $\mathcal{A}$ is strongly dense in the unit ball $Ball_1(\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$ of $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$
the set of selfadjoint elements in $Ball_1(\mathcal{A})$ is strongly dense in the set of selfadjoint elements of $Ball_1(\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$
nodes.label: TheoremKaplansky

nodes.name: approximate-unit criterion for orthogonal functionals
nodes.statement: Let $\phi$ and $\psi$ be two positive linear functionals on $\mathcal{A}$. Then, $\phi\perp\psi$ if and only if for all $\epsilon>0$ there exists a positive element $a\in\mathcal{A}$ with norm less than or equal to $1$, such that $\phi(e-a)<\epsilon$ and $\psi(a)<\epsilon$.
assumptions: $\phi$ and $\psi$ be two positive linear functionals on $\mathcal{A}$
conclusions: $\phi\perp\psi$ if and only if for all $\epsilon>0$ there exists a positive element $a\in\mathcal{A}$ with norm less than or equal to $1$, such that $\phi(e-a)<\epsilon$ and $\psi(a)<\epsilon$
nodes.label: phiperppsi

nodes.name: orthogonality passes to dominated functionals
nodes.statement: Let $\phi_1$, $\phi_2$, $\psi_1$ and $\psi_2$ be positive linear functionals on $\mathcal{A}$ such that $\phi_1\leq\phi_2$ and $\psi_1\leq\psi_2$. If $\phi_2\perp\psi_2$, then $\phi_1\perp\psi_1$.
assumptions: $\phi_1$, $\phi_2$, $\psi_1$ and $\psi_2$ be positive linear functionals on $\mathcal{A}$ such that $\phi_1\leq\phi_2$ and $\psi_1\leq\psi_2$
conclusions: $\phi_1\perp\psi_1$
nodes.label: phi1lessthanphi2perppsi1lessthatpsi2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.13
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma_1>0$ and $\gamma_2>0$ be such that $\gamma_1\phi_2-\phi_1$ and $\gamma_2\psi_2-\psi_1$ are positive. By Fact \ref{phiperppsi}, for $\epsilon>0$ there exists a positive $a\in\mathcal{A}$ with norm less than or equal to $1$ such that $\phi_2(e-a)<\frac{\epsilon}{\gamma_1+\gamma_2}$ and $\psi_2(a)<\frac{\epsilon}{\gamma_1+\gamma_2}$. Then $\phi_1(e-a)\leq\gamma_1\phi_2(e-a)<\frac{\gamma_1\epsilon}{\gamma_1+\gamma_2}<\epsilon$ and $\psi_1(a)\leq\gamma_2\psi_2(a)<\frac{\gamma_2\epsilon}{\gamma_1+\gamma_2}<\epsilon$.
nodes.statement_short: Use the criterion of Fact 4.12 with $\epsilon/(\gamma_1+\gamma_2)$ and the domination constants.

nodes.name: orthogonal functionals iff disjoint cyclic representations
nodes.statement: Let $v,w\in H$. $\phi_v\perp\phi_w$ if and only if no subrepresentation of $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$.
conclusions: $\phi_v\perp\phi_w$ if and only if no subrepresentation of $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$
nodes.label: HvperpHw

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.14
nodes.statement: Suppose $\phi_v\perp\phi_w$. By Lemma \ref{phi1lessthanphi2perppsi1lessthatpsi2}, if $(H_{v^\prime},\pi_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$ is a subrepresentation of $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ and $(H_{w^\prime},\pi_{w^\prime},w^\prime)$ is a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$, then $\phi_{v^\prime}\perp\phi_{w^\prime}$, By Lemma \ref{phivperpphiwnotismoetricallyisomorphic}, $(H_{v^\prime},\pi_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$ is not isometrically isomorphic to $(H_{w^\prime},\pi_{w^\prime},w^\prime)$, and the conclusion follows. Conversely, suppose no subrepresentation of $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$. Then the representations $(H_v,\pi_v)$ and $(H_w,\pi_w)$ are disjoint. By Fact \ref{FactDisjointSubrepresentationsHaveDisjointProjections}, there is a projection $P\in\pi(\mathcal{A})^\prime\cap\pi(\mathcal{A})^{\prime\prime}$ such that $PP_v=P_v$ and $(I-P)P_w=P_w$. Then, $\phi_v(I-P)=\langle (I-P)v\ |\ v\rangle=\langle (v-PP_vv)\ |\ v\rangle=\langle (v-v)\ |\ v\rangle=0$. On the other hand, $\phi_w(P)=\langle Pw\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-(w-Pw)\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-(I-P)w\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-(I-P)P_ww\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-P_ww\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-w\ |\ w\rangle=0$. By Fact \ref{FactMMisDoubleCommutantOfPiOfA} and Theorem \ref{TheoremKaplansky}, the projection $P$ is strongly approximable by positive elements in $\pi(\mathcal{A})$ and therefore, for $\epsilon>0$ there exists a positive element $a\in\mathcal{A}$ with norm less than or equal to $1$, such that $\phi_v(e-a)<\epsilon$ and $\phi_w(a)<\epsilon$. By Fact \ref{phiperppsi}, $\phi_v\perp\phi_w$.
nodes.statement_short: Forward via Lemmas 4.13 and 4.7. Converse: disjointness gives a central projection separating $v$ and $w$, approximated by positive elements via Kaplansky density, then Fact 4.12.

nodes.name: almost orthogonality of 1-types over $\emptyset$
nodes.statement: Let $p,q\in S_1(\emptyset)$, let $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p$ and $w\models q$. Then, $p\perp^a q$ if and only if $\phi_{v_e}\perp \phi_{w_e}$.
assumptions: $p,q\in S_1(\emptyset)$, let $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p$ and $w\models q$
conclusions: $p\perp^a q$ if and only if $\phi_{v_e}\perp \phi_{w_e}$

nodes.name: almost orthogonality of 1-types over $E$
nodes.statement: Let $E\subseteq H$. Let $p,q\in S_1(E)$, let $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p$ and $w\models q$. Then, $p\perp_E^a q$ if and only if $\phi_{P^\perp_E(v_e)}\perp \phi_{P^\perp_E(w_e)}$
assumptions: $E\subseteq H$. Let $p,q\in S_1(E)$, let $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p$ and $w\models q$
conclusions: $p\perp_E^a q$ if and only if $\phi_{P^\perp_E(v_e)}\perp \phi_{P^\perp_E(w_e)}$

nodes.statement: Clear by Lemma \ref{orthogonalityoverempty}.

nodes.name: almost orthogonality equals orthogonality
nodes.statement: Let $E\subseteq H$. Let $p,q\in S_1(E)$. Then, $p\perp^a q$ if and only if $p\perp q$.
conclusions: $p\perp^a q$ if and only if $p\perp q$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.17
nodes.statement: Assume $p\perp^a q$, $E\subseteq F\subseteq H$ are small subsets of the monster model and $p^\prime$, $q^\prime\in S_1(F)$ are non-forking extensions of $p$ and $q$ respectively. Let $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p^\prime$ and $w\models q^\prime$, then $\phi_{P^\perp_F(v_e)}=\phi_{P^\perp_Ev_e}\perp\phi_{P^\perp_Ew_e}=\phi_{P^\perp_F(w_e)}$. By Lemma \ref{orthogonalityoverempty}, this implies that $p^\prime\perp^a q^\prime$. Therefore $p\perp q$. The converse is trivial.
nodes.statement_short: Nonforking extensions keep the relevant projected functionals, so almost orthogonality persists to every nonforking extension; converse trivial.

nodes.name: domination of 1-types over $\emptyset$
nodes.statement: Let $p,q\in S_1(\emptyset)$ and let $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p$ and $w\models q$. Then, $p\vartriangleright_\emptyset q$ if and only if $\phi_{w_e}\leq\phi_{v_e}$.
assumptions: $p,q\in S_1(\emptyset)$ and let $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p$ and $w\models q$
conclusions: $p\vartriangleright_\emptyset q$ if and only if $\phi_{w_e}\leq\phi_{v_e}$
nodes.label: dominationoverempty

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.18
nodes.statement: Suppose $p\vartriangleright_\emptyset q$. Suppose that $v^\prime$ and $w^\prime$ are such that $v^\prime\models p$, $w^ \prime\models q$ and if $v^\prime\ind^*_\emptyset E$ then $w^\prime\ind_\emptyset^*E$ for every $E$. Then for every $E\subseteq H$ \[P_Ev^\prime_e=0\Rightarrow P_Ew^\prime_e=0\] This implies that $w^\prime_e\in H_{v^\prime_e}$, and $H_{w^\prime_e}\subseteq H_{v^\prime_e}$. By Theorem \ref{HvinHw}, $\phi_{w_e}=\phi_{w^\prime_e}\leq\phi_{v^\prime_e}=\phi_{v_e}$. For the converse, suppose $\phi_{w_e}\leq\phi_{v_e}$. Then, by Theorem \ref{HvinHw} $H_{w_e}$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $H_{v_e}$, which implies that there is $w^\prime\in H_v$ such that $w^\prime\models tp(w/\emptyset)$ and for every $E\subseteq H$ \[P_Ev_e=0\Rightarrow P_Ew^\prime_e=0\] This means than $tp(w/\emptyset)\vartriangleleft_\emptyset tp(v/\emptyset)$.
nodes.statement_short: Domination forces $w'_e\in H_{v'_e}$, then Theorem 4.5 gives $\phi_{w_e}\leq\phi_{v_e}$; conversely Theorem 4.5 embeds $H_{w_e}$ into $H_{v_e}$.

nodes.name: domination of stationary 1-types
nodes.statement: Let $E$, $F$ and $G$ be small subsets of $\tilde{H}$ such that $E$, $F\subseteq G$ and $p\in S_1(E)$ and $q\in S_1(F)$ be two stationary types. Then $p\vartriangleright_G q$ if and only if there exist $v$, $w\in\tilde{H}$ such that $tp(v/G)$ is a non-forking extension of $p$, $tp(w/G)$ is a non-forking extension of $q$ and $\phi_{P^\perp_{acl(G)}w_e}\leq\phi_{P^\perp_{acl(G)}v_e}$.
nodes.statement_short: $p$ dominates $q$ over $G$ iff some nonforking extensions to $G$ have realizations whose projected essential functionals satisfy $\phi_{w}\leq\phi_{v}$.
assumptions: $E$, $F$ and $G$ be small subsets of $\tilde{H}$ such that $E$, $F\subseteq G$ and $p\in S_1(E)$ and $q\in S_1(F)$ be two stationary types
conclusions: $p\vartriangleright_G q$ if and only if there exist $v$, $w\in\tilde{H}$ such that $tp(v/G)$ is a non-forking extension of $p$, $tp(w/G)$ is a non-forking extension of $q$ and $\phi_{P^\perp_{acl(G)}w_e}\leq\phi_{P^\perp_{acl(G)}v_e}$
nodes.label: dominationoverA

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.19
nodes.statement: Clear by Lemma \ref{dominationoverempty}.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from Lemma 4.18.

nodes.name: large sum
nodes.statement: Let $\kappa>2^{\aleph_0}$ and consider $(H,\pi)\oplus\bigoplus_{i\in I}(H_e,\pi_e)$. By Corollary \ref{CoroElementaryEquivalent}.
nodes.statement_short: Consider the sum with many copies of $(H_e,\pi_e)$, elementarily equivalent by Corollary 2.5.

nodes.name: many realizations
nodes.statement: Then there are $\kappa$ vectors $v_i$ for $i<\kappa$ such that every $v_i$ has the same type over $\emptyset$ as $v$.
nodes.statement_short: Get $\kappa$ realizations of $tp(v/\emptyset)$.

nodes.name: unbounded orbit
nodes.statement: This means that the orbit of $v$ under the automorphisms of $(H,\pi)$ is unbounded and therefore $v$ is not algebraic over the emptyset.
nodes.statement_short: Unbounded orbit so $v$ is not algebraic.

nodes.name: split v
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be the Hilbert subspace of $H$ generated by $dcl(E)$ and $acl(\emptyset)$. It is clear that $G\subseteq acl(E)$. Let $v\in acl(E)$. By Lemma \ref{Hdsubsetalgebraicclosureofemptyset}, $v_d\in acl(\emptyset)$, and by Theorem \ref{definclosure} and Lemma \ref{Henotalgebraicoveremptyset}, $v_e\in dcl(E)\setminus acl(\emptyset)$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $G\subseteq acl(E)$; for $v\in acl(E)$ place $v_d$ in $acl(\emptyset)$ and $v_e$ in $dcl(E)$.

nodes.name: conclude
nodes.statement: Then $v_e\in dcl(E)$ and $acl(E)\subseteq G$.
nodes.statement_short: Hence $acl(E)\subseteq G$.

nodes.name: reduce to 1-tuples
nodes.statement: By Remark \ref{RemarkItIsEnoughIndependenceForOneVector}, to prove local character, finite character and transitivity it is enough to show them for the case of a 1-tuple.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce local character, finite character and transitivity to 1-tuples.

nodes.name: Local character
nodes.statement: [Local character] Let $v\in H$ and $E\subseteq H$. Let $w=(P_{acl(E)}(v))_e$. Then there exist a sequence of $(l_k)_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}\subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$, a sequence of finite tuples $(a_1^k,\dots,a_{l_k}^k)_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}\subseteq \mathcal{A}$ and a sequence of finite tuples $(e_1^k,\dots,e_{l_k}^k)_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}\subseteq E$ such that if $w_k:=\sum_{j=1}^{l_k}\pi(a_j^k)e_j^k$ for $k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$, then $w_k\to w$ when $k\to\infty$. Let $E_0=\{e_j^k\ |\ j=1,\dots,l_k\text{ and }k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}\}$. Then $v\ind_{E_0}^*E$ and $|E_0|=\aleph_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Local character: a countable $E_0\subseteq E$ suffices.

nodes.name: introduce w
nodes.statement: Let $v\in H$ and $E\subseteq H$. Let $w=(P_{acl(E)}(v))_e$.
nodes.statement_short: Let $w$ be the essential part of the projection onto $acl(E)$.

nodes.name: approximate w
nodes.statement: Then there exist a sequence of $(l_k)_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}\subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$, a sequence of finite tuples $(a_1^k,\dots,a_{l_k}^k)_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}\subseteq \mathcal{A}$ and a sequence of finite tuples $(e_1^k,\dots,e_{l_k}^k)_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}\subseteq E$ such that if $w_k:=\sum_{j=1}^{l_k}\pi(a_j^k)e_j^k$ for $k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$, then $w_k\to w$ when $k\to\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Approximate $w$ by finite combinations $\sum\pi(a)e$ with $e\in E$.

nodes.name: countable base
nodes.statement: Let $E_0=\{e_j^k\ |\ j=1,\dots,l_k\text{ and }k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}\}$. Then $v\ind_{E_0}^*E$ and $|E_0|=\aleph_0$.
nodes.statement_short: The countable set $E_0$ of used elements witnesses local character.

nodes.name: Finite character
nodes.statement:
[Finite character] We show that for $v\in H$, $E,F\subseteq H$, $v\ind^*_EF$ if and only if $v\ind^*_EF_0$ for every finite $F_0\subseteq F$. The left to right direction is clear. For right to left, suppose that $v
ind^*_EF$. Let $w=P_{acl(E\cup F)}(v)-P_{acl(E)}(v)$. Then $w\in$ acl$(E\cup F)\setminus$acl$(E)$. As in the proof of local character, there exist a sequence of pairs $(l_k,n_k)_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}\subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}^2$, a sequence of finite tuples $(a_1^k,\dots,a_{l_k+n_k}^k)_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}\subseteq \mathcal{A}$ and a sequence of finite tuples $(e_1^k,\dots,e_{l_k}^k,f_1^k,\dots,f_{n_k}^k)_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}$ such that $(e_1^k,\dots,e_{l_k}^k)\subseteq E$, $(f_1^k,\dots,f_{n_k}^k)_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}\subseteq F$ and if $w_k:=\sum_{j=1}^{l_k}\pi(a_j^k)e_i^k+\sum_{j=1}^{n_k}\pi(a_{l_k+j}^k)f_j^k$ for $k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$, then $w_k	o w$ when $k	o\infty$. Since $v
ind^*_EF$, then $w=P_{acl(E\cup F)}(v)-P_{acl(E)}(v)
eq 0$. Let $\epsilon=\|w\|>0$. Then, there is $k_\epsilon$ such that if $k\geq k_\epsilon$ then $\|w-w_k\|<\epsilon$. Let $F_0:=\{f_1^1,\dots,f_{k_\epsilon}^{n_{k_\epsilon}}\}$, then $F_0$ is a finite subset such that $v
ind^*_EF_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Finite character: a dependence is witnessed by a finite subset.

nodes.name: statement and easy direction
nodes.statement: [Finite character] We show that for $v\in H$, $E,F\subseteq H$, $v\ind^*_EF$ if and only if $v\ind^*_EF_0$ for every finite $F_0\subseteq F$. The left to right direction is clear.
nodes.statement_short: State finite character; left-to-right is clear.

nodes.name: assume dependence
nodes.statement: For right to left, suppose that $v\nind^*_EF$. Let $w=P_{acl(E\cup F)}(v)-P_{acl(E)}(v)$. Then $w\in$ acl$(E\cup F)\setminus$acl$(E)$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume dependence and set $w$ the difference of projections.

nodes.name: approximate w
nodes.statement: As in the proof of local character, there exist a sequence of pairs $(l_k,n_k)_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}\subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}^2$, a sequence of finite tuples $(a_1^k,\dots,a_{l_k+n_k}^k)_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}\subseteq \mathcal{A}$ and a sequence of finite tuples $(e_1^k,\dots,e_{l_k}^k,f_1^k,\dots,f_{n_k}^k)_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}$ such that $(e_1^k,\dots,e_{l_k}^k)\subseteq E$, $(f_1^k,\dots,f_{n_k}^k)_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}\subseteq F$ and if $w_k:=\sum_{j=1}^{l_k}\pi(a_j^k)e_i^k+\sum_{j=1}^{n_k}\pi(a_{l_k+j}^k)f_j^k$ for $k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$, then $w_k\to w$ when $k\to\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Approximate $w$ by finite combinations from $E$ and $F$.

nodes.name: finite witness
nodes.statement:
Since $v
ind^*_EF$, then $w=P_{acl(E\cup F)}(v)-P_{acl(E)}(v)
eq 0$. Let $\epsilon=\|w\|>0$. Then, there is $k_\epsilon$ such that if $k\geq k_\epsilon$ then $\|w-w_k\|<\epsilon$. Let $F_0:=\{f_1^1,\dots,f_{k_\epsilon}^{n_{k_\epsilon}}\}$, then $F_0$ is a finite subset such that $v
ind^*_EF_0$.
nodes.statement_short: A close enough approximation yields a finite $F_0$ witnessing dependence.

nodes.name: Transitivity
nodes.statement: [Transitivity of independence] Let $v\in H$ and $E\subseteq F\subseteq G\subseteq H$. If $v\ind_E^*G$ then $P_{acl(E)}(v)=P_{acl(G)}(v)$. It is clear that $P_{acl(E)}(v)=P_{acl(F)}(v)=P_{acl(G)}(v)$ so $v\ind_E^*F$ and $v\ind_F^*G$. Conversely, if $v\ind_E^*F$ and $v\ind_F^*G$, we have that $P_{acl(E)}(v)=P_{acl(F)}(v)$ and $P_{acl(F)}(v)=P_{acl(G)}(v)$. Then $P_{acl(E)}(v)=P_{acl(G)}(v)$ and $v\ind_E^*G$.
nodes.statement_short: Transitivity: equality of projections is transitive.

nodes.name: forward
nodes.statement: Let $v\in H$ and $E\subseteq F\subseteq G\subseteq H$. If $v\ind_E^*G$ then $P_{acl(E)}(v)=P_{acl(G)}(v)$. It is clear that $P_{acl(E)}(v)=P_{acl(F)}(v)=P_{acl(G)}(v)$ so $v\ind_E^*F$ and $v\ind_F^*G$.
nodes.statement_short: From $v\ind^*_EG$ get both $v\ind^*_EF$ and $v\ind^*_FG$.

nodes.name: converse
nodes.statement: Conversely, if $v\ind_E^*F$ and $v\ind_F^*G$, we have that $P_{acl(E)}(v)=P_{acl(F)}(v)$ and $P_{acl(F)}(v)=P_{acl(G)}(v)$. Then $P_{acl(E)}(v)=P_{acl(G)}(v)$ and $v\ind_E^*G$.
nodes.statement_short: Chain the equal projections for the converse.

nodes.name: Symmetry
nodes.statement: [Symmetry] It is clear from Remark \ref{independenceoverA}.
nodes.statement_short: Symmetry from Remark 3.2.

nodes.name: Invariance
nodes.statement: [Invariance] Let $U$ be an automorphism of $(H,\pi)$. Let $\bar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n)$,$\bar w=(w_1,\dots,w_n)\in H^n$ and $E\subseteq H$ be such that $\bar v\ind_E^*\bar w$. By Remark \ref{independenceoverA}, this means that for every $j$, $k=1,\dots,n$ $H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}(v_j)}\perp H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}(w_k)}$. It follows that for every $j$, $k=1,\dots,n$ $H_{P^\perp_{acl(UE)}(Uv_j)}\perp H_{P^\perp_{acl(UE)}(Uw_k)}$ and, again by Remark \ref{independenceoverA}, $Uv\ind_{acl(UE)}^*Uw$.
nodes.statement_short: Invariance: automorphisms preserve the orthogonality of the cyclic subspaces.

nodes.name: rewrite as orthogonality
nodes.statement: [Invariance] Let $U$ be an automorphism of $(H,\pi)$. Let $\bar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n)$,$\bar w=(w_1,\dots,w_n)\in H^n$ and $E\subseteq H$ be such that $\bar v\ind_E^*\bar w$. By Remark \ref{independenceoverA}, this means that for every $j$, $k=1,\dots,n$ $H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}(v_j)}\perp H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}(w_k)}$.
nodes.statement_short: By Remark 3.2 independence means orthogonality of cyclic subspaces.

nodes.name: transport
nodes.statement: It follows that for every $j$, $k=1,\dots,n$ $H_{P^\perp_{acl(UE)}(Uv_j)}\perp H_{P^\perp_{acl(UE)}(Uw_k)}$ and, again by Remark \ref{independenceoverA}, $Uv\ind_{acl(UE)}^*Uw$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply $U$ and use Remark 3.2 again.

nodes.name: Existence
nodes.statement: [Existence] Let $(\tilde{H},\tilde{\pi})$ be the monster model and let $E\subseteq F\subseteq \tilde{H}$ be small sets. We show, by induction on $n$, that for every $p\in S_n(E)$, there exists $q\in S_n(F)$ such that $q$ is a non-forking extension of $p$. \begin{description} \item[Case $n=1$] Let $v\in \tilde{H}$ be such that $p=tp(v/E)$ and let $(H^\prime,\pi^\prime,u):=(H_{(P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)},\pi_{(P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)},P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)$. Then, by Fact \ref{HensonsLemma}, the model $(\hat{H},\hat{\pi}):=(H,\pi)\oplus (H^\prime,\pi^\prime)$ is an elementary extension of $(H,\pi)$. Let $v^\prime:=P_{acl(E)}v+P^\perp_{acl(E)}v_d+u\in \hat{H}$. Then, by Theorem \ref{nonforkingextension}, the type $tp(v^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v/E)$. \item[Induction step] Now, let $\bar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1})\in \tilde{H}^{n+1}$. By induction hypothesis, there are $v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime\in H$ such that $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n/E)$. Let $U$ be an automorphism of the monster model fixing $E$ pointwise such that for every $j=1,\dots,n$, $U(v_j)=v_j^\prime$. Let $v_{n+1}^\prime\in \tilde{H}$ be such that $tp(v_{n+1}^\prime/Fv_1^\prime\cdots v_n^\prime)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(U(v_{n+1})/Ev_1^\prime,\cdots v_n^\prime)$. Then, by transitivity, $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime,v_{n+1}^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1}/E)$.
nodes.statement_short: Existence of nonforking extensions by induction on $n$.

nodes.name: set up induction
nodes.statement: [Existence] Let $(\tilde{H},\tilde{\pi})$ be the monster model and let $E\subseteq F\subseteq \tilde{H}$ be small sets. We show, by induction on $n$, that for every $p\in S_n(E)$, there exists $q\in S_n(F)$ such that $q$ is a non-forking extension of $p$.
nodes.statement_short: Set up induction on the length $n$.

nodes.name: case n=1
nodes.statement: [Case $n=1$] Let $v\in \tilde{H}$ be such that $p=tp(v/E)$ and let $(H^\prime,\pi^\prime,u):=(H_{(P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)},\pi_{(P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)},P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)$. Then, by Fact \ref{HensonsLemma}, the model $(\hat{H},\hat{\pi}):=(H,\pi)\oplus (H^\prime,\pi^\prime)$ is an elementary extension of $(H,\pi)$. Let $v^\prime:=P_{acl(E)}v+P^\perp_{acl(E)}v_d+u\in \hat{H}$. Then, by Theorem \ref{nonforkingextension}, the type $tp(v^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v/E)$.
nodes.statement_short: Base case: add an orthogonal copy of the cyclic representation via Henson's lemma and use Theorem 3.4.

nodes.name: induction step
nodes.statement: [Induction step] Now, let $\bar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1})\in \tilde{H}^{n+1}$. By induction hypothesis, there are $v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime\in H$ such that $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n/E)$. Let $U$ be an automorphism of the monster model fixing $E$ pointwise such that for every $j=1,\dots,n$, $U(v_j)=v_j^\prime$. Let $v_{n+1}^\prime\in \tilde{H}$ be such that $tp(v_{n+1}^\prime/Fv_1^\prime\cdots v_n^\prime)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(U(v_{n+1})/Ev_1^\prime,\cdots v_n^\prime)$. Then, by transitivity, $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime,v_{n+1}^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1}/E)$.
nodes.statement_short: Extend the first $n$ coordinates, move by an automorphism, extend the last, conclude by transitivity.

nodes.name: Stationarity
nodes.statement: [Stationarity] Let $(\tilde{H},\tilde{\pi})$ be the monster model and let $E\subseteq F\subseteq \tilde{H}$ be small sets. We show, by induction on $n$, that for every $p\in S_n(E)$, if $q\in S_n(F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $p$ to $F$ then $q=p^\prime$, where $p^\prime$ is the $\ind^*$-independent extension of $p$ to $F$ built in the proof of existence. \begin{description} \item[Case $n=1$] Let $v\in H$ be such that $p=tp(v/E)$, and let $q\in S(F)$ and $w\in H$ be such that $w\models q$. Let $v^\prime$ be as in previous item. Then, by Theorem \ref{nonforkingextension} we have that: \begin{enumerate} \item $P_{acl(E)}v=P_{acl(F)}v^\prime=P_{acl(F)}w$ \item $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v},P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to both \[(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},P^\perp_{acl(F)}w)\] and \[(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime)\] \end{enumerate} This means that $P_{acl(F)}v^\prime=P_{acl(F)}w$ and $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},P^\perp_{acl(F)}w)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime)$ and, therefore $q=tp(v^\prime/F)=p^\prime$. \item[Induction step] Let $\bar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1})$, $\bar v^\prime=(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1}^\prime)$ and $\bar w=(w_1,\dots,w_{n+1})\in\tilde{H}$ be such that $\bar v\models p$, $\bar v^\prime\models p^\prime$ and $\bar w\models q$. By transitivity, we have that $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime/F)$ and $tp(w_1,\dots,w_n/F)$ are $\ind^*$-independent extensions of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n/E)$. By induction hypothesis, $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime/F)=tp(w_1,\dots,w_n/F)$. Let $U$ be an automorphism of the monster model fixing $E$ pointwise such that for every $j=1,\dots,n$, $U(v_j)=v_j^\prime$ and let $U^\prime$ an automorphism of the monster model fixing $F$ pointwise such that for every $j=1,\dots,n$, $U^\prime(v_j^\prime)=w_j^\prime$. Again by transitivity, $tp(U^{-1}(v_{n+1}^\prime)/Fv_1\cdots v_n)$ and $tp((U^\prime\circ U)^{-1}(w_{n+1})/Fv_1,\cdots v_n)$ are $\ind^*$-independent extensions of $tp(v_{n+1}/Ev_1,\cdots v_n)$. By the case $n=1$ $tp(U^{-1}(v_{n+1}^\prime)/Fv_1\cdots v_n)=tp((U^\prime\circ U)^{-1}(w_{n+1})/Fv_1,\cdots v_n)$ and therefore $p^\prime=tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime v_{n+1}^\prime/F)=tp(w_1,\dots,w_n,w_{n+1}/F)=q$.
nodes.statement_short: Stationarity: the independent extension is unique, by induction on $n$.

nodes.name: set up induction
nodes.statement: [Stationarity] Let $(\tilde{H},\tilde{\pi})$ be the monster model and let $E\subseteq F\subseteq \tilde{H}$ be small sets. We show, by induction on $n$, that for every $p\in S_n(E)$, if $q\in S_n(F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $p$ to $F$ then $q=p^\prime$, where $p^\prime$ is the $\ind^*$-independent extension of $p$ to $F$ built in the proof of existence.
nodes.statement_short: Set up induction showing any independent extension equals the constructed one.

nodes.name: case n=1
nodes.statement: [Case $n=1$] Let $v\in H$ be such that $p=tp(v/E)$, and let $q\in S(F)$ and $w\in H$ be such that $w\models q$. Let $v^\prime$ be as in previous item. Then, by Theorem \ref{nonforkingextension} we have that: \begin{enumerate} \item $P_{acl(E)}v=P_{acl(F)}v^\prime=P_{acl(F)}w$ \item $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v},P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to both \[(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},P^\perp_{acl(F)}w)\] and \[(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime)\] \end{enumerate} This means that $P_{acl(F)}v^\prime=P_{acl(F)}w$ and $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},P^\perp_{acl(F)}w)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime)$ and, therefore $q=tp(v^\prime/F)=p^\prime$.
nodes.statement_short: Base case: Theorem 3.4 gives the same projections and isomorphic cyclic representations, so the types agree.

nodes.name: induction step
nodes.statement: [Induction step] Let $\bar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1})$, $\bar v^\prime=(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1}^\prime)$ and $\bar w=(w_1,\dots,w_{n+1})\in\tilde{H}$ be such that $\bar v\models p$, $\bar v^\prime\models p^\prime$ and $\bar w\models q$. By transitivity, we have that $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime/F)$ and $tp(w_1,\dots,w_n/F)$ are $\ind^*$-independent extensions of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n/E)$. By induction hypothesis, $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime/F)=tp(w_1,\dots,w_n/F)$. Let $U$ be an automorphism of the monster model fixing $E$ pointwise such that for every $j=1,\dots,n$, $U(v_j)=v_j^\prime$ and let $U^\prime$ an automorphism of the monster model fixing $F$ pointwise such that for every $j=1,\dots,n$, $U^\prime(v_j^\prime)=w_j^\prime$. Again by transitivity, $tp(U^{-1}(v_{n+1}^\prime)/Fv_1\cdots v_n)$ and $tp((U^\prime\circ U)^{-1}(w_{n+1})/Fv_1,\cdots v_n)$ are $\ind^*$-independent extensions of $tp(v_{n+1}/Ev_1,\cdots v_n)$. By the case $n=1$ $tp(U^{-1}(v_{n+1}^\prime)/Fv_1\cdots v_n)=tp((U^\prime\circ U)^{-1}(w_{n+1})/Fv_1,\cdots v_n)$ and therefore $p^\prime=tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime v_{n+1}^\prime/F)=tp(w_1,\dots,w_n,w_{n+1}/F)=q$.
nodes.statement_short: Use the induction hypothesis, automorphisms and the case $n=1$.

nodes.name: stability
nodes.statement: By Fact \ref{LemmaTstableIffItHasGoodIndependenceRelation}, $T_\pi$ is stable and the relation $\ind^*$ agrees with non-forking.
nodes.statement_short: Stability and agreement with nonforking from Fact 3.7.

nodes.name: what superstability needs
nodes.statement: To prove superstability, we have to show that for every $\bar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n)\in H$, every $F\subseteq H$ and every $\epsilon>0$, there exist a finite $F_0\subseteq F$ and $\bar v^\prime=(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime)\in H^n$ such that $\|v_j-v_j^\prime\|<\epsilon$ and $v_j^\prime\ind_{F_0}F$ for every $j\leq n$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce superstability to finite-base approximation of tuples.

nodes.name: approximations
nodes.statement: As in the proof of local character, for $j=1,\dots,n$ let $(\ a_1^{jk},\dots,\ a_{l_k}^{jk})_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}$, $(\ e_1^{jk},\dots,\ e_{l_k}^{jk})_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}$, $w_j:=(P_{acl(E)}(v_j))_e$ and $(w_j^k)_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}$ be such that $w_j^k:=\sum_{s=1}^{l_k}\pi(a_s^{jk})\ e_s^{jk}$ for $k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$, and $w_j^k\to w_j$. For $j=1,\dots,n$, let $K_j\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$ be such that $\|w_j-w_j^{K_j}\|<\epsilon$, let $v_j^\prime:=(P_{acl(E)}v_j)_d+w_j^{K_j}$ and let $F_0^j=\{e_s^k\ |\ k\leq K_j\text{ and }s=1,\dots,l_k\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Approximate each $w_j$ by finite combinations and choose truncation levels $K_j$.

nodes.name: finite base
nodes.statement: If we define $F_0:=U_{j=1}^nF_0^j$, then for every $j=1,\dots,n$ we have that $v_j^\prime\ind_{F_0}^*F$, $|F_0|<\aleph_0$ and $\|v_j-v_j^\prime\|<\epsilon$.
nodes.statement_short: The finite union $F_0$ works.

nodes.name: does not fork over Cb
nodes.statement: First of all, we consider the case of a 1-tuple. By Theorem \ref{nonforkingextension} $tp(v/E)$ does not fork over $Cb(tp(v/E))$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to 1-tuples; nonforking over $Cb$ by Theorem 3.4.

nodes.name: Morley sequence
nodes.statement: Let $(v_k)_{k<\omega}$ a Morley sequence for $tp(v/E)$. We have to show that $P_Ev\in dcl((v_k)_{k<\omega})$.
nodes.statement_short: Take a Morley sequence; must show $P_Ev$ is definable from it.

nodes.name: decompose
nodes.statement: By Theorem \ref{nonforkingextension}, for every $k<\omega$ there is a vector $w_k$ such that $v_k=P_Ev+w_k$ and $w_k\perp acl(\{P_Ev\}\cup\{w_j\ |\ j< k\})$. This means that for every $k<\omega$, $w_k\in H_e$ and for all $j$, $k<\omega$, $H_{w_j}\perp H_{w_k}$.
nodes.statement_short: Write $v_k=P_Ev+w_k$ with mutually orthogonal essential $w_k$.

nodes.name: averages
nodes.statement: For $k<\omega$, let $v^\prime_k:=\frac{v_1+\cdots+v_k}{n}=P_Ev+\frac{w_1+\cdots+w_k}{n}$. Then for every $k<\omega$, $v^\prime_k\in dcl((v_k)_{k<\omega})$.
nodes.statement_short: Averages of the sequence are definable from it.

nodes.name: limit
nodes.statement: Since $v^\prime_k\to P_ev$ when $k\to\infty$, we have that $P_Ev\in dcl((v_k)_{k<\omega})$.
nodes.statement_short: Averages converge to $P_Ev$, so it is definable.

nodes.name: n-tuples
nodes.statement: For the case of a general $n$-tuple, by Remark \ref{RemarkItIsEnoughIndependenceForOneVector}, it is enough to repeat the previous argument in every component of $\bar v$.
nodes.statement_short: General tuples coordinatewise by Remark 3.2.

nodes.name: embedding
nodes.statement: Suppose $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$. Then there exists a vector $v^\prime\in H_w$ such that $(H_v,\pi_v,v)\simeq (H_{v^\prime},\pi_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume an embedding; get $v'\in H_w$ with the same cyclic representation.

nodes.name: Radon-Nikodym
nodes.statement: By Radon Nikodim Theorem for rings of operators (see \cite{Hen}), there exists a bounded positive operator $P:(H_w,\pi_w,w)\to (H_{v^\prime},\pi_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$ such that $Pw=v^\prime$ and $P$ commutes with every element of $\pi_v(\mathcal{A})$.
nodes.statement_short: Radon-Nikodym gives a positive operator $P$ with $Pw=v'$.

nodes.name: estimate
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma=\|P\|^2$. Then, for every positive element $a\in\mathcal{A}$, $\phi_{v}(a)=\phi_{v^\prime}(a)=\langle \pi(a)v^\prime\ |\ v^\prime\rangle=\langle \pi(a)Pw\ |\ Pw\rangle=\langle P^*\pi(a)Pw\ |\ w\rangle=\langle \pi(a)\|P\|^2w\ |\ w\rangle\leq \gamma\langle \pi(a)w\ |\ w\rangle=\gamma\phi_{w}(a)$ which means that $\gamma\phi_w-\phi_{v}$ is positive and $\phi_v\leq\phi_w$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\phi_v\leq\|P\|^2\phi_w$.

nodes.name: converse
nodes.statement: The converse is Corollary 3.3.8 in \cite{Pe}.
nodes.statement_short: Converse cited from Pedersen.

nodes.name: assume
nodes.statement: Suppose $\phi_v\perp\phi_w$, and $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume orthogonal and embeddable.

nodes.name: domination and GNS
nodes.statement: By Theorem \ref{HvinHw} $\phi_v\leq\phi_w$; let $\gamma>0$ be a real number such that $\gamma\phi_w-\phi_v$ is a bounded positive functional and let $u\in H$ be such that $\phi_u=\gamma\phi_w-\phi_v$, which is possible by GNS Theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Get $\gamma$ and $u$ with $\phi_u=\gamma\phi_w-\phi_v$.

nodes.name: contradiction
nodes.statement: Then $\phi_v=\gamma\phi_w-\phi_u$, and $\|\phi_w-\phi_v\|=\|\phi_w-\gamma\phi_w+\phi_u\|=\|(1-\gamma)\phi_w+\phi_u\|=|1-\gamma|\|\phi_w\|+\|\phi_u\|\neq \|\phi_w\|+\|\phi_v\|$, but this contradicts $\phi_v\perp\phi_w$.
nodes.statement_short: The norm computation contradicts orthogonality.

nodes.name: choose a
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma_1>0$ and $\gamma_2>0$ be such that $\gamma_1\phi_2-\phi_1$ and $\gamma_2\psi_2-\psi_1$ are positive. By Fact \ref{phiperppsi}, for $\epsilon>0$ there exists a positive $a\in\mathcal{A}$ with norm less than or equal to $1$ such that $\phi_2(e-a)<\frac{\epsilon}{\gamma_1+\gamma_2}$ and $\psi_2(a)<\frac{\epsilon}{\gamma_1+\gamma_2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Take domination constants and apply Fact 4.12 to $\phi_2,\psi_2$.

nodes.name: transfer
nodes.statement: Then $\phi_1(e-a)\leq\gamma_1\phi_2(e-a)<\frac{\gamma_1\epsilon}{\gamma_1+\gamma_2}<\epsilon$ and $\psi_1(a)\leq\gamma_2\psi_2(a)<\frac{\gamma_2\epsilon}{\gamma_1+\gamma_2}<\epsilon$.
nodes.statement_short: The same $a$ works for $\phi_1,\psi_1$.

nodes.name: forward
nodes.statement: Suppose $\phi_v\perp\phi_w$. By Lemma \ref{phi1lessthanphi2perppsi1lessthatpsi2}, if $(H_{v^\prime},\pi_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$ is a subrepresentation of $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ and $(H_{w^\prime},\pi_{w^\prime},w^\prime)$ is a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$, then $\phi_{v^\prime}\perp\phi_{w^\prime}$, By Lemma \ref{phivperpphiwnotismoetricallyisomorphic}, $(H_{v^\prime},\pi_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$ is not isometrically isomorphic to $(H_{w^\prime},\pi_{w^\prime},w^\prime)$, and the conclusion follows.
nodes.statement_short: Forward: sub-functionals stay orthogonal (Lemma 4.13), so no isomorphic subrepresentations (Lemma 4.7).

nodes.name: converse
nodes.statement: Conversely, suppose no subrepresentation of $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$. Then the representations $(H_v,\pi_v)$ and $(H_w,\pi_w)$ are disjoint. By Fact \ref{FactDisjointSubrepresentationsHaveDisjointProjections}, there is a projection $P\in\pi(\mathcal{A})^\prime\cap\pi(\mathcal{A})^{\prime\prime}$ such that $PP_v=P_v$ and $(I-P)P_w=P_w$. Then, $\phi_v(I-P)=\langle (I-P)v\ |\ v\rangle=\langle (v-PP_vv)\ |\ v\rangle=\langle (v-v)\ |\ v\rangle=0$. On the other hand, $\phi_w(P)=\langle Pw\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-(w-Pw)\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-(I-P)w\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-(I-P)P_ww\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-P_ww\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-w\ |\ w\rangle=0$. By Fact \ref{FactMMisDoubleCommutantOfPiOfA} and Theorem \ref{TheoremKaplansky}, the projection $P$ is strongly approximable by positive elements in $\pi(\mathcal{A})$ and therefore, for $\epsilon>0$ there exists a positive element $a\in\mathcal{A}$ with norm less than or equal to $1$, such that $\phi_v(e-a)<\epsilon$ and $\phi_w(a)<\epsilon$. By Fact \ref{phiperppsi}, $\phi_v\perp\phi_w$.
nodes.statement_short: Converse via a separating central projection.

nodes.name: disjoint
nodes.statement: Conversely, suppose no subrepresentation of $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$. Then the representations $(H_v,\pi_v)$ and $(H_w,\pi_w)$ are disjoint.
nodes.statement_short: The cyclic representations are disjoint.

nodes.name: projection
nodes.statement: By Fact \ref{FactDisjointSubrepresentationsHaveDisjointProjections}, there is a projection $P\in\pi(\mathcal{A})^\prime\cap\pi(\mathcal{A})^{\prime\prime}$ such that $PP_v=P_v$ and $(I-P)P_w=P_w$.
nodes.statement_short: Fact 4.9 gives a central projection $P$.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.statement: Then, $\phi_v(I-P)=\langle (I-P)v\ |\ v\rangle=\langle (v-PP_vv)\ |\ v\rangle=\langle (v-v)\ |\ v\rangle=0$. On the other hand, $\phi_w(P)=\langle Pw\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-(w-Pw)\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-(I-P)w\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-(I-P)P_ww\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-P_ww\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-w\ |\ w\rangle=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Compute $\phi_v(I-P)=0$ and $\phi_w(P)=0$.

nodes.name: approximate
nodes.statement: By Fact \ref{FactMMisDoubleCommutantOfPiOfA} and Theorem \ref{TheoremKaplansky}, the projection $P$ is strongly approximable by positive elements in $\pi(\mathcal{A})$ and therefore, for $\epsilon>0$ there exists a positive element $a\in\mathcal{A}$ with norm less than or equal to $1$, such that $\phi_v(e-a)<\epsilon$ and $\phi_w(a)<\epsilon$.
nodes.statement_short: Kaplansky density approximates $P$ by positive elements.

nodes.name: conclude
nodes.statement: By Fact \ref{phiperppsi}, $\phi_v\perp\phi_w$.
nodes.statement_short: Fact 4.12 gives orthogonality.

nodes.name: forward
nodes.statement: Suppose $p\perp^a q$. By Remark \ref{independenceoverempty}, this implies that $H_{v_e}\perp H_{w_e}$ for all $v\models p$ and $w\models q$. Let $v\models p$ and $w\models q$. Then no subrepresentation of $(H_{v_e},\pi_{v_e},v_e)$ is isometrically isomorphic to any subrepresentation of $(H_{w_e},\pi_{w_e},w_e)$. By Lemma \ref{HvperpHw}, this implies that $\phi_{v_e}\perp \phi_{w_e}$.
nodes.statement_short: Forward: orthogonal cyclic subspaces, then Theorem 4.14.

nodes.name: orthogonal subspaces
nodes.statement: Suppose $p\perp^a q$. By Remark \ref{independenceoverempty}, this implies that $H_{v_e}\perp H_{w_e}$ for all $v\models p$ and $w\models q$.
nodes.statement_short: Remark 3.2 gives $H_{v_e}\perp H_{w_e}$.

nodes.name: no common subrepresentation
nodes.statement: Let $v\models p$ and $w\models q$. Then no subrepresentation of $(H_{v_e},\pi_{v_e},v_e)$ is isometrically isomorphic to any subrepresentation of $(H_{w_e},\pi_{w_e},w_e)$.
nodes.statement_short: Hence no common subrepresentations.

nodes.name: apply theorem
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{HvperpHw}, this implies that $\phi_{v_e}\perp \phi_{w_e}$.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 4.14 gives orthogonal functionals.

nodes.name: non-orthogonal realizations
nodes.statement: Conversely, if $p\not\perp^a q$ there are $v$, $w\in H$ such that $v\models p$, $w\models q$ and $H_{v_e}\not\perp H_{w_e}$.

nodes.name: common dominated functional
nodes.statement: Since $v_e=P_{w_e}v_e+P_{w_e}^\perp v_e$ and $P_{w_e}v_e\neq 0$, we can prove that $\phi_{P_{w_e}v_e}\leq \phi_{v_e}$ by using a procedure similar to the one used in the proof of Theorem \ref{HvinHw} and, since $P_{w_e}v_e\in H_{w_e}$, we get $\phi_{P_{w_e}v_e}\leq \phi_{w_e}$.

nodes.name: conclude

nodes.name: assume
nodes.statement: Assume $p\perp^a q$, $E\subseteq F\subseteq H$ are small subsets of the monster model and $p^\prime$, $q^\prime\in S_1(F)$ are non-forking extensions of $p$ and $q$ respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Take nonforking extensions to $F$.

nodes.name: functionals preserved
nodes.statement: Let $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p^\prime$ and $w\models q^\prime$, then $\phi_{P^\perp_F(v_e)}=\phi_{P^\perp_Ev_e}\perp\phi_{P^\perp_Ew_e}=\phi_{P^\perp_F(w_e)}$. By Lemma \ref{orthogonalityoverempty}, this implies that $p^\prime\perp^a q^\prime$. Therefore $p\perp q$. The converse is trivial.
nodes.statement_short: Projected functionals are unchanged under nonforking extension, so the extensions are almost orthogonal by Lemma 4.15; converse trivial.

nodes.name: forward
nodes.statement: Suppose $p\vartriangleright_\emptyset q$. Suppose that $v^\prime$ and $w^\prime$ are such that $v^\prime\models p$, $w^ \prime\models q$ and if $v^\prime\ind^*_\emptyset E$ then $w^\prime\ind_\emptyset^*E$ for every $E$. Then for every $E\subseteq H$ \[P_Ev^\prime_e=0\Rightarrow P_Ew^\prime_e=0\] This implies that $w^\prime_e\in H_{v^\prime_e}$, and $H_{w^\prime_e}\subseteq H_{v^\prime_e}$. By Theorem \ref{HvinHw}, $\phi_{w_e}=\phi_{w^\prime_e}\leq\phi_{v^\prime_e}=\phi_{v_e}$.
nodes.statement_short: Forward: domination forces $w'_e\in H_{v'_e}$, then Theorem 4.5.

nodes.name: witnesses
nodes.statement: Suppose $p\vartriangleright_\emptyset q$. Suppose that $v^\prime$ and $w^\prime$ are such that $v^\prime\models p$, $w^ \prime\models q$ and if $v^\prime\ind^*_\emptyset E$ then $w^\prime\ind_\emptyset^*E$ for every $E$.
nodes.statement_short: Take realizations witnessing domination.

nodes.name: containment
nodes.statement: Then for every $E\subseteq H$ \[P_Ev^\prime_e=0\Rightarrow P_Ew^\prime_e=0\] This implies that $w^\prime_e\in H_{v^\prime_e}$, and $H_{w^\prime_e}\subseteq H_{v^\prime_e}$.
nodes.statement_short: Projections vanish together, so $H_{w'_e}\subseteq H_{v'_e}$.

nodes.name: apply theorem
nodes.statement: By Theorem \ref{HvinHw}, $\phi_{w_e}=\phi_{w^\prime_e}\leq\phi_{v^\prime_e}=\phi_{v_e}$.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 4.5 gives the inequality of functionals.

nodes.name: converse
nodes.statement: For the converse, suppose $\phi_{w_e}\leq\phi_{v_e}$. Then, by Theorem \ref{HvinHw} $H_{w_e}$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $H_{v_e}$, which implies that there is $w^\prime\in H_v$ such that $w^\prime\models tp(w/\emptyset)$ and for every $E\subseteq H$ \[P_Ev_e=0\Rightarrow P_Ew^\prime_e=0\] This means than $tp(w/\emptyset)\vartriangleleft_\emptyset tp(v/\emptyset)$.
nodes.statement_short: Converse: Theorem 4.5 embeds $H_{w_e}$ in $H_{v_e}$, giving domination.
